title: Population structure caveats
dek: Shared ancestry associates genotypes with each other and often with phenotypes. If you ignore it, every lineage-tagging SNP inherits a confounder fork.
story: Two isolates that share a recent ancestor share thousands of SNPs and often share a phenotype (resistance, virulence, geography). That is confounding by ancestry, the fork plate with U = relatedness. A naive GLM of Y on G treats those SNPs as independent experiments.

Standard repairs: include PCs of the genotype matrix as C, or a random effect u ~ N(0, τ² K) with K a kinship/realised relatedness matrix (LMM). Neither is magic if the causal mechanism is itself collinear with ancestry (a lineage-defining resistance mutation).

Bacterial populations are often clonal with occasional recombination. Human PCs-as-covariates folklore does not transfer unchanged. A phylogeny, a linear mixed model on a SNP-distance K, or a within-lineage scan are the usual TB moves. Report which, and which isolates were too close to count as two experiments.
deepTitle: What PCs and K actually model
deep: PCs: the leading eigenvectors of a genotype covariance. Putting them in the mean is an additive adjustment for axes of variation. If structure is a tree with long branches, a few PCs can be a crude summary; leftover relatedness still inflates λ_GC.

LMM: Y = Xβ + u + ε, Var(u) = τ² K. This is the mixed-model plate with a specific G. It partial-pools similar isolates. The score test for a SNP then uses that V. You still should not test a SNP that was used to build K without a leave-one-chromosome-out (or leave-one-locus-out) discipline — circularity.
Over-correction: adjusting for lineage when the scientific question is “does this lineage have higher MIC?” deletes the signal. Structure control is relative to an estimand. Write the estimand.
Transmission studies want relatedness as the object, not the nuisance. That is the phylogenetics plates. Using a GWAS LMM there is answering a different question.

formulas.label: Kinship LMM (Gaussian sketch)
formulas.expression: Y = Xβ + u + ε,   u ~ N(0, τ² K),   ε ~ N(0, σ² I)
formulas.note: K = realised relatedness. Binary Y uses a GLMM / PQL / score-test cousin.

formulas.label: PC adjustment
formulas.expression: g(E[Y|G, PC]) = β_G G + ∑_{k=1}^K γ_k PC_k + ⋯
formulas.note: A low-rank mean adjustment, not a full kinship.

visual.caption: Ancestry as nested relatedness: species / major lineage / outbreak cluster / isolate. SNPs shared at each level are not independent tests of a phenotype that also sits on those levels. PCs approximate the top cuts; a kinship or tree models more of the ladder.

example.title: Two outbreak isolates are not two experiments
example.setup: 220 genomes, but 40 are a single MDR outbreak differing by <5 SNPs. Phenotype: fluoroquinolone MIC. A SNP present in the outbreak is perfectly correlated with being in the outbreak.

steps.title: Naive n
steps.body: Software says n = 220. The outbreak SNP’s “n” is closer to 1 cluster plus 180 other isolates.

steps.title: K or collapse
steps.body: A kinship LMM down-weights near-duplicates. Or analyse one representative per cluster as a sensitivity check. If the association dies, it was clonality.

steps.title: If the mutation is gyrA S91P in the outbreak
steps.body: It may still be causal for MIC and also a tag of the outbreak. Within-outbreak variation (heteroresistance, later acquisition) is the extra evidence. Structure control cannot invent that variation.

example.takeaway: Relatedness is a confounder of association and a reducer of effective n. Model it, or stop claiming n = number of fasta files.

check.prompt: Ignoring population structure in a SNP–phenotype GLM is primarily a:
choices: Confounding problem: ancestry is a common cause of genotype and often of phenotype
check.answer: Confounding problem: ancestry is a common cause of genotype and often of phenotype
check.why: The fork U→G and U→Y. Multiplicity is a separate bill.

whyWrong.Proof that Bonferroni is enough: FWER does not close a backdoor.

check.prompt: 40 near-duplicate outbreak isolates plus 10 diverse isolates. Treating n=50 iid overstates independent samples. A crude “one per cluster” n is closest to:
check.why: 1 outbreak cluster + 10 others = 11. Kinship LMM is a softer version of this count.

check.prompt: On the relatedness hierarchy, isolates sit at the bottom. Why is that layer labelled “not iid”?
choices: Because fasta files are independent by definition
Because isolates in a cluster share ancestry, so their (G, Y) pairs are dependent experiments
Because PCs require iid SNPs only
check.answer: Because isolates in a cluster share ancestry, so their (G, Y) pairs are dependent experiments
check.why: That is the plate’s warning. K or a tree is how you stop pretending iid.

whyWrong.Because PCs require iid SNPs only: PCs are a tool, not the reason.
